sections.heading: What Is a Video Compressor?
sections.body:
A video compressor is a tool that reduces the amount of data required to store a video.

Digital videos contain a sequence of frames, along with audio and other possible streams. Their file size depends on factors such as resolution, bitrate, duration, frame rate, codec and visual complexity.

Video compression uses encoding methods to represent this information more efficiently.

FileCompresser uses H.264 video encoding to prepare compatible video files in the MP4 container. This format is commonly used for sharing, website playback and everyday video storage.

However, compression does not guarantee that every output will be smaller. The final result depends on the original video and the selected settings.

sections.heading: How to Compress a Video Online
sections.body:
You can use FileCompresser to prepare a supported video without installing desktop software.

Follow these steps:

1. Open the Video Compressor page.
2. Select an MP4 or MOV video from your device.
3. Wait for the website to validate the file.
4. Choose the desired resolution setting.
5. Start video processing.
6. Allow the browser to encode the video.
7. Download the resulting MP4.
8. Play the complete video and check its quality.

Keep your original video until you have confirmed that the new file plays correctly.

sections.heading: Understand Video Resolution Settings
sections.body: Resolution describes the number of pixels used to display a video. Higher resolutions contain more image detail but can also require more data. FileCompresser provides different maximum-height options.

sections.heading: Keep Original
sections.body:
Keep Original maintains the original video dimensions. Choose this option when you do not want to reduce the display resolution.

However, H.264 encoding may require even dimensions. If the source has odd dimensions, the encoder may need a suitable explicitly selected resolution cap.

sections.heading: 1080p
sections.body: A 1080p maximum-height setting can be useful for videos that need to retain a relatively high level of detail while allowing larger inputs to be reduced.

sections.heading: 720p
sections.body: 720p can be suitable for everyday sharing, presentations and general online viewing when full HD resolution is not necessary.

sections.heading: 480p
sections.body:
480p provides a lower resolution option for situations where smaller dimensions are acceptable.

The tool does not enlarge smaller input videos. Always select a resolution based on how the final video will be viewed.

sections.heading: What Is H.264 Video Encoding?
sections.body:
H.264 is a widely used video compression standard. It allows video information to be encoded in a format supported by many devices and applications.

FileCompresser uses H.264 for its MP4 output. When the source contains audio, the output uses AAC audio encoding.

This combination is commonly used for everyday video sharing and playback.

A file's extension alone does not guarantee that its original codec is supported. A video may have an MP4 or MOV extension but still contain an unsupported video stream. In that situation, the tool may reject the source.

sections.heading: Why Should You Compress Video Files?
sections.body: Video compression is useful for many everyday tasks.

sections.heading: Share Videos More Easily
sections.body: Large video files can be difficult to send through email or messaging services. A smaller MP4 may be easier to transfer.

sections.heading: Prepare Videos for Websites
sections.body: Website owners and content publishers often use videos to explain services, demonstrate products or share tutorials. Reducing unnecessary video data can help manage storage and page resources.

sections.heading: Save Device Storage
sections.body: Smartphones and computers can quickly fill up with recorded videos. Creating smaller copies may help manage storage space.

sections.heading: Upload Videos to Online Platforms
sections.body: Some platforms have maximum file size requirements. Video compression can help prepare compatible files for uploading.

sections.heading: Prepare Videos for Presentations
sections.body: Business presentations and educational material sometimes include video clips. Smaller files can make presentations easier to store and transfer.

sections.heading: Does Video Compression Reduce Quality?
sections.body:
Video re-encoding can affect image and audio quality.

The final appearance depends on the original recording, selected resolution and encoding process. Lowering resolution can remove image detail, while stronger compression can affect textures, movement and small text.

Audio may also change during conversion.

For this reason, always play the complete output before sharing it. Check important scenes, movement, spoken words and sound quality. Keep the original recording if you may need to edit it again or create another export.

sections.heading: Why Does the First Video Take Longer?
sections.body:
The first video, audio or GIF processing job loads the required WebAssembly version of FFmpeg. This processing engine is approximately 21 MB and may be cached by your browser for later use.

Video encoding also requires processing power and memory. Long recordings and high-resolution videos can take considerable time, even when the input is within the stated file limit.

FileCompresser accepts video files up to 200 MiB per file. Media jobs have a five-minute processing limit. If a job fails, try a shorter clip or select a lower resolution.

sections.heading: Which Video Information Is Retained?
sections.body:
The tool focuses on the primary video and audio streams. Subtitles and cover art are not retained in the output.

If your video depends on embedded subtitles or additional streams, keep the original file and use a workflow that supports those elements.

After processing, check the MP4 in your preferred video player to confirm that the required picture and sound are present.

sections.heading: Private Video Processing in Your Browser
sections.body: FileCompresser processes selected videos directly on your device. Your video is not uploaded to the website's servers for conversion. Your browser memory, available processing power and video duration can affect the result.

sections.heading: Compress Videos for Easier Sharing
sections.body:
Large video files can create problems when uploading, storing or sharing recordings. A suitable compression setting can help make these files more manageable.

FileCompresser provides an online way to convert supported MP4 and MOV videos into H.264 MP4 files. Choose the resolution that matches your requirements, process your video and check the complete output before downloading.
